chunks: Aban narrated from Mansur, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who bought goods in which there is no measurement by volume nor weight. May he sell them as murabahah before taking possession of them and take his profit?
He عليه السلام said: There is no harm in that so long as there is no measurement by volume nor weight in it. But if he takes possession of it, then that is more freeing of liability for himself.

key_terms.أَبْرَأُ: safer and more free from liability
key_terms.رِبْحَهُ: the profit taken from the resale
key_terms.كَيْلٌ: measurement by volume in commercial sale
key_terms.مُرَابَحَةً: a sale made with a declared profit margin
key_terms.وَزْنٌ: measurement by weight in commercial sale
key_terms.يَقْبِضَهُ: to take possession of the purchased goods

ai.seo_question: Can a person sell goods at a profit before taking possession if they are not sold by weight or measure?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on selling purchased goods at a profit before taking possession of them. It permits this in cases where the goods are not of the kind sold by measure or weight, while stating that taking possession first is safer and more prudent for the seller.
